% CONCLUSION. Numbers ONLY via \R... macros.
Marginal context value profiles measure, per model and task family, how much each kind of context changes success.
A budget compiler can then act on them with certificates and millisecond latency. In a pre-registered local evaluation
the compiled context did not beat embedding relevance in area under the success--budget curve, and it lost on history
because its block-level ranker learned recency instead of relevance. It did reduce prompt tokens at a non-binding budget (a hypothesis added before testing) by
\RTokCutTool on tool use and \RTokCutHistory on history without losing success, and its profiles exposed which context
types were worth sending at all. We release the method, data adapters, logs and analysis so that the profiles, and the
negative result, can be checked and extended.

\textbf{Use of AI assistance.} An AI coding assistant was used to write and test code, run the experiments, and draft
and edit text. All numbers in the paper are generated from the released logs by scripts, and every reference was
verified against its DOI record. The author reviewed the content and is responsible for it.

\textbf{Artifact availability.} The \texttt{mcv} package, data adapters (with the licenses of HotpotQA and BFCL),
pre-registration, raw logs of every model call, and the scripts that regenerate all figures, tables and numbers with one
command will be released under an open license with the preprint.
